name: New Composition
description: Creates a new composition with chosen resolution, frame rate and duration — the canvas every animation lives in. Start an archviz film by setting comps to your delivery format, typically 3840x2160 at 25 fps.

name: Composition Settings
description: Edits the current comp's size, duration, frame rate and background colour after creation. Revisit it when a client changes delivery specs mid-project.

name: Precompose
description: Wraps the selected layers into a nested composition so they can be treated, animated and effected as one unit. Essential housekeeping — precompose each animated diagram or title block before the timeline becomes unmanageable.

name: Import File
description: Brings footage, image sequences, PSDs and audio into the Project panel. Import rendered archviz sequences as image sequences so dropped frames can be re-rendered individually.

name: Add Footage to Comp
description: Drops the selected Project panel items into the active composition as new layers. Quicker than dragging when building comps from many rendered passes.

name: Increment and Save
description: Saves the project under an automatically numbered new filename, keeping the previous version intact. Use it before risky restructuring — version discipline saves animation projects.

name: Save Frame As
description: Sends the current frame to the render queue as a still image. Handy for pulling high-quality stills of an animation for portfolio boards or client emails.

name: New Solid
description: Creates a flat colour layer used as a background, a matte or a host for generated effects like Fractal Noise. Most effect-driven elements in a motion piece start life as a solid.

name: Solid Settings
description: Changes the colour and dimensions of an existing solid layer. Use Make Comp Size here when a background solid needs to fill the frame exactly.

name: New Adjustment Layer
description: Creates an invisible layer whose effects apply to everything below it. The standard way to grade a whole archviz shot with Lumetri or add global glow without touching individual layers.

name: New Null Object
description: Creates an invisible control layer that other layers can be parented to. Animate one null to move a whole cluster of labels, leader lines and highlights together.

name: New Text Layer
description: Creates an empty text layer ready for typing, with full animator controls for per-character animation. The starting point for titles, statistics call-outs and room labels in an archviz film.

name: New Shape Layer
description: Creates a vector layer built from paths, fills and strokes, with procedural operators like Trim Paths and Repeater. The engine behind animated diagrams, growing site outlines and self-drawing linework.

name: Pen Tool
description: Draws Bézier paths that become masks on footage layers or paths on shape layers. Use it to trace a building outline for a reveal or to mask a sky for replacement.

name: Shape and Mask Tools
description: Cycles through the rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse, polygon and star tools for drawing shapes or masks. Which you get depends on whether a footage or shape layer is selected.

name: Duplicate Layer
description: Copies the selected layer in place with all its keyframes, effects and masks. The everyday way to build variations — duplicate a label animation and just retype the text.

name: Split Layer
description: Cuts the selected layer at the current time into two independent layers. Use it to change treatment halfway through a shot or remove a bad section of footage.

name: Trim Layer In/Out
menu: Alt+[ or Alt+] at the current-time indicator
description: Trims the selected layer's in or out point to the current time without moving the footage. The fast way to tidy layer bars so the timeline reads like a clean storyboard.

name: Move Layer to Current Time
description: Slides the selected layer so its in point ( [ ) or out point ( ] ) lands at the current-time indicator. Useful for choreographing staggered entrances of labels and diagram elements.

name: Sequence Layers
description: Arranges the selected layers end to end in time, optionally with overlapping crossfades. Perfect for turning a folder of still renders into a quick animatic slideshow.

name: Time-Reverse Layer
description: Plays the selected layer backwards. A classic trick for build-up animations — animate a structure exploding apart, then reverse it so it assembles.

name: Lock Layer
description: Locks the selected layers against selection and edits. Lock finished background plates so late tweaks cannot disturb them.

name: Solo Layer
description: Displays only the soloed layers in the viewer, hiding everything else. Invaluable for isolating one element of a dense composite while adjusting it.

name: Shy Layers
menu: Timeline shy switches and comp Hide Shy toggle
description: Marks layers as shy and then hides them from the timeline list without removing them from the render. Use it to collapse dozens of finished background layers and keep only active work visible.

name: Fit Layer to Comp
description: Scales the selected layer to match the composition frame exactly. Quick framing for full-screen background plates; beware it will stretch mismatched aspect ratios.

name: Show Position
description: Reveals just the Position property of selected layers in the timeline. The property shortcuts (P, S, R, T, A) keep the timeline lean while animating.

name: Show Scale
description: Reveals the Scale property of selected layers. Combine with held Shift to add further properties to the same view.

name: Show Rotation
description: Reveals the Rotation property, plus orientation values on 3D layers. Reach for it when animating turntable-style spins of a model or compass needles on diagrams.

name: Show Opacity
description: Reveals the Opacity property of selected layers. Opacity keyframes are the humble backbone of most fade-based archviz transitions.

name: Show Anchor Point
description: Reveals the Anchor Point property, the pivot around which scale and rotation act. Move the anchor to a building's base before scaling it up so it grows from the ground.

name: Pan Behind Tool
description: Drags the anchor point on the canvas without moving the layer's rendered position. The clean way to re-pivot a layer before animating rotation or growth.

name: Show Animated Properties
description: Reveals every property that carries keyframes on the selected layers. Press it twice (UU) to also show any modified properties and expressions — the fastest way to read how someone else's comp works.

name: Show Effects
description: Reveals the effects applied to selected layers in the timeline; EE reveals expressions only. Handy for tweaking effect keyframes without opening the Effect Controls panel.

name: Add Keyframe at Current Time
description: Adds a keyframe for a transform property at the current time without touching the mouse, enabling the stopwatch if needed. Part of a fast keyboard-only animation workflow.

name: Easy Ease
description: Smooths the selected keyframes so motion accelerates and decelerates naturally instead of starting and stopping abruptly. The single biggest instant upgrade to any camera move or element animation.

name: Easy Ease In / Out
description: Applies easing to only the incoming (Shift+F9) or outgoing (Ctrl+Shift+F9) side of the selected keyframes. Use them to make an element ease to a stop but leave sharply.

name: Graph Editor
description: Switches the timeline to value and speed curves you can sculpt directly, giving precise control over acceleration. Where good camera moves become great — flatten the speed curve tails for silky drone-style glides.

name: Keyframe Velocity
description: Sets numeric incoming and outgoing speed and influence for the selected keyframe. Useful when several shots must share identical easing values for a consistent house style.

name: Keyframe Interpolation
description: Changes selected keyframes between linear, Bézier and hold interpolation, spatially and temporally. Fix curved position paths that should travel straight by setting spatial interpolation to linear.

name: Toggle Hold Keyframe
description: Freezes a keyframe's value until the next keyframe, with no interpolation between. Use holds for stepped diagrams — phasing plans that snap from stage to stage.

name: Next / Previous Keyframe
description: Jumps the current-time indicator to the previous (J) or next (K) visible keyframe. Keeps you landing exactly on keyframes when adjusting values, avoiding accidental in-between keys.

name: Motion Blur
menu: Layer motion blur switch + comp Enable Motion Blur
description: Renders realistic blur on fast-moving layers when both the layer switch and the comp toggle are on. Enable it on animated labels and fast camera moves so motion feels filmed rather than pasted.

name: Parent with Pick Whip
description: Drags the spiral pick whip from one layer to another so the child inherits the parent's transforms. Build rigs this way — parent all annotation layers to one null and move the lot together.

name: Auto-Orient
description: Makes a layer rotate automatically along its motion path, or a camera face its point of interest. Useful for arrows tracing a route through a site plan.

name: Go to Time
description: Moves the current-time indicator to an exact timecode you type. Precision matters when syncing animation hits to a music track's beats.

name: Set Work Area
menu: B and N keys at the current time
description: Sets the start (B) and end (N) of the work area, the range used for previews and optional render trimming. Keep the work area tight around the section you are iterating on to preview faster.

name: Trim Comp to Work Area
menu: Composition > Trim Comp to Work Area
description: Shortens the composition's duration to match the current work area. Tidy finishing move once a shot's final length is decided.

name: Preview
description: Plays the composition from the current time, caching frames into RAM as it goes. Watch the green cached bar — once the work area is fully cached, playback is real-time.

name: Step One Frame
menu: Page Down / Page Up (or Ctrl+Right / Ctrl+Left)
description: Advances or rewinds the current-time indicator a single frame; add Shift to jump ten. Frame-stepping is how you check that an ease lands exactly where intended.

name: Go to Layer In / Out Point
menu: I and O keys with a layer selected
description: Jumps the current-time indicator to the selected layer's in point (I) or out point (O). Pairs naturally with the trim shortcuts when conforming layers to a beat.

name: Enable Time Remapping
description: Adds a keyframeable Time Remap property so you can speed up, slow down, freeze or reverse footage over time. The tool behind elegant speed ramps in walkthrough animations.

name: Time Stretch
description: Changes a layer's overall playback speed by a percentage, lengthening or shortening it uniformly. Use it to conform a rendered flythrough to the length the music demands.

name: Frame Blending
menu: Layer frame blending switch + comp toggle
description: Synthesises in-between frames when footage is slowed down, using frame mix or the higher-quality pixel motion mode. Turn it on to stop retimed footage stuttering.

name: New Mask
description: Adds a full-frame rectangular mask to the selected layer, ready to be reshaped. Masks confine a layer to a region — the basis of reveals, split screens and sky replacements.

name: Mask Feather
menu: Press F with a masked layer selected
description: Reveals the Mask Feather property, which softens the mask edge by a settable amount. Feathered masks blend a graded region invisibly into the surrounding footage.

name: Show Mask Properties
menu: Press M or MM with a masked layer selected
description: Reveals the mask path (M) or every mask property including feather, opacity and expansion (MM). Keyframe the mask path itself to animate a wipe that follows a building edge.

name: Track Matte
description: Uses another layer's alpha or luminance to cut the visibility of the layer below, without merging them. The standard mechanism for text-shaped reveals and map-shaped footage windows.

name: Roto Brush Tool
description: Paints strokes over a subject and lets After Effects propagate the selection through the shot, separating foreground from background. Use it to isolate people walking through footage so graphics can pass behind them.

name: Effects & Presets Panel
description: Searches every effect and animation preset by name and applies them by double-click or drag. Learn to type-search here rather than trawling the Effect menu's categories.

name: Effect Controls Panel
description: Shows and edits the parameters of every effect on the selected layer. Your main dashboard while grading, blurring or distorting a shot.

name: Apply Last Effect
menu: Effect > (last effect at top of menu)
description: Reapplies the most recently used effect to the current selection. Speeds up applying the same treatment across a batch of shots.

name: Remove All Effects
description: Strips every effect from the selected layers in one go. A clean reset when an experimental grading stack has gone muddy.

name: Glow Effect
description: Brightens and blooms the brightest areas of a layer, simulating light spill. A staple for making evening render windows and light fittings feel luminous.

name: Curves Effect
description: Remaps tonal values along an editable curve, per channel if needed. The precision tool for lifting shadows in a dark interior render or adding gentle contrast.

name: Lumetri Colour Effect
description: A full grading suite — exposure, colour wheels, HSL secondaries, LUTs and vignettes — in a single effect. Apply it to an adjustment layer to give a whole sequence a coherent cinematic grade.

name: Fractal Noise Effect
description: Generates evolving procedural noise used for fog, clouds, water shimmer and animated textures. Animate its Evolution property on a solid to add drifting atmosphere over a static render.

name: Displacement Map Effect
description: Shifts a layer's pixels based on the luminance of another layer. Drive it with fractal noise for heat-haze or rippling water reflections in front of a facade.

name: Fast Box Blur Effect
menu: Effect > Blur & Sharpen > Fast Box Blur
description: An efficient blur with iterations for smoother falloff. Blur a duplicated background plate to fake shallow depth of field behind foreground titles.

name: Gradient Ramp Effect
description: Fills a layer with a linear or radial gradient between two colours. Applied to a solid, it makes quick skies, vignettes and background washes for diagram scenes.

name: 3D Layer Switch
description: Converts a 2D layer into a 3D layer with position, rotation and material properties in three axes. Flick it on to arrange plans, sections and photos in space for a parallax fly-through.

name: New Camera
description: Adds a camera layer that views the 3D layers in the comp, with real lens parameters like focal length and depth of field. One animated camera gliding past layered drawings instantly elevates a portfolio film.

name: Unified Camera Tool
description: Orbits, pans and dollies the 3D view with the three mouse buttons; pressing C cycles the individual camera tools. Use it to compose 3D shots interactively before keyframing the camera.

name: New Light
description: Adds a point, spot, parallel or ambient light that illuminates 3D layers and can cast shadows. Combine a soft spot with layer shadows to give floating drawings physical presence.

name: Material Options
menu: Press AA with a 3D layer selected
description: Reveals a 3D layer's material properties — whether it casts and accepts shadows, and how it responds to lights. Tune these when a layered 3D collage needs believable shadowing.

name: 3D Camera Tracker
menu: Effect > Perspective > 3D Camera Tracker (or Animation > Track Camera)
description: Analyses footage to reconstruct the original camera move, letting you pin 3D text and graphics into the scene. The key to locking project labels onto drone footage of a site.

name: Track Motion
description: Follows a feature through footage and applies its movement to another layer or a stabilisation. Use it to pin a callout to a window that drifts through a handheld shot.

name: Warp Stabiliser
description: Automatically removes camera shake from footage, with options from smooth motion to a fully locked shot. First aid for handheld site footage before it goes anywhere near a client film.

name: Add Expression
description: Attaches a small script to a property so its value is computed rather than keyframed; Alt+clicking the stopwatch does the same. The gateway to procedural animation — start by linking one property to another.

name: Wiggle Expression
description: Adds continuous random variation to a property — wiggle(2, 15) on position gives a gentle handheld drift. Sparingly applied to a camera or light, it stops digital moves feeling sterile.

name: Loop Expression
description: Repeats a property's keyframes indefinitely — cycle, ping-pong or continue modes — without duplicating them. Ideal for endlessly rotating sun-path diagrams or pulsing highlight markers.

name: Add to Render Queue
description: Queues the active composition for rendering inside After Effects, with render settings and output modules per item. Use it for lossless masters and image-sequence outputs.

name: Add to Media Encoder Queue
menu: Composition > Add to Adobe Media Encoder Queue
description: Sends the comp to Adobe Media Encoder for background encoding to delivery formats like H.264. Lets you keep working in After Effects while client-review MP4s render.

name: Output Module Settings
description: Sets the format, codec, channels and post-render actions for a queued render, including alpha output. Choose a format with an alpha channel when rendering overlays destined for an edit.

name: Pre-render
description: Renders a heavy comp to disk and substitutes the movie as a proxy, so downstream comps stop recalculating it. Reach for it when a nested particle or 3D comp is strangling preview speed.

name: Create Proxy
description: Generates a low-resolution stand-in for heavy footage that After Effects uses for previews but swaps out at render time. Essential when cutting 4K render sequences on a modest workstation.

name: Collect Files
description: Copies the project and every asset it uses into one folder for archiving or handover. The After Effects equivalent of packaging an InDesign document — run it before archiving a finished film.

name: Zoom Viewer In / Out
menu: , and . keys over the Composition panel
description: Zooms the composition viewer out (,) and in (.) around the view centre. Note this changes your view only — layer scale is untouched.

name: Fit View
description: Fits the composition into the viewer at up to 100 percent zoom. The quick reset after working zoomed into a corner of the frame.

name: Hand Tool
description: Pans the view within the Composition panel; holding the spacebar gives the same behaviour temporarily. Everyday navigation while inspecting details of a frame.

name: Take Snapshot
description: Stores the current frame in memory; hold F5 to flash it back over the viewer for comparison. Perfect for before-and-after checks while grading a shot.

name: Show Rulers
description: Toggles rulers around the composition viewer, from which guides can be dragged. Useful when aligning lower-third titles to a consistent margin across shots.

name: Show Guides
description: Toggles visibility of guides dragged from the rulers. Set up title-safe margins for text placement and keep every caption on the same lines.

name: Show Grid
description: Overlays a non-rendering grid on the composition viewer for alignment. Helpful when laying out arrays of small diagrams or aligning multi-panel comparisons.

name: Toggle Transparency Grid
menu: Composition panel Toggle Transparency Grid button
description: Replaces the comp background with a chequerboard so genuine transparency is visible. Check it before rendering overlays with alpha for the edit suite.

name: Viewer Resolution
menu: Composition panel resolution menu (Full / Half / Quarter)
description: Drops the preview resolution to speed up interaction and caching without affecting the final render. Work at Half on heavy comps and flick to Full only for quality checks.

name: Region of Interest
menu: Composition panel Region of Interest button
description: Restricts rendering to a drawn rectangle of the frame, cutting preview times dramatically. Draw it around the one element you are tweaking in an otherwise heavy shot.

name: Project Panel
description: Toggles the Project panel, where all imported footage, solids and comps live in folders. Keep it ruthlessly organised — a films-worth of unlabelled comps is a maintenance nightmare.
